passage:
Anjali, you asked why I went quiet last spring. I'm Elizabeth, and I couldn't sleep, because I didn't know what my feelings meant: who I liked, and how, and whether I should be afraid of the answer. I googled at two in the morning, which only made it noisier. I told myself I had to pick a word for it right now.
Then the school librarian noticed me standing at the shelf too long and said there's no deadline on labels. They handed me a book from a reliable youth organisation. And you didn't ask me anything, you just kept sitting with me at lunch.
The fear didn't vanish, but it got smaller. I'm still figuring it out, and I'm okay with that.

qa.q: At what time was Elizabeth googling?
qa.a: Elizabeth was googling at two in the morning.

qa.q: What was Elizabeth afraid of during that spring?
qa.a: Elizabeth was afraid of what the feelings meant and of the answer, and felt a label was needed right away.

qa.q: What helped Elizabeth feel less afraid?
qa.a: Elizabeth heard there is no deadline on labels, got reliable information from the librarian and had Anjali's quiet company at lunch.

qa.q: How might Anjali have seen those quiet lunches?
qa.a: Anjali showed acceptance by sitting with Elizabeth without asking questions, which helped Elizabeth feel safe.

grounding: Shows a teen unsure about who they are and their feelings of attraction, afraid, finding no deadline for labels, safe people and reliable information.

passage: The counsellor's room at St Joseph's had a dripping air conditioner and a jar of mints nobody ate. Saurabh sat turning a mint over in his fingers for five minutes before he spoke. 'I don't know what's wrong with me. My friend Tejas... when he talks to a girl, I feel weird. Jealous. Not a friend kind of jealous. And then I'm scared I'm... I don't even know the word.' The counsellor, Mrs Pillai, didn't flinch. 'Nothing's wrong with you, Saurabh. Lots of people your age feel unsure about who they're drawn to. You don't have to pick a label today, or this year.' He let out a breath he hadn't known he was holding. She wrote down a helpline run by trained counsellors and the name of a book in the school library, instead of the random videos he'd been watching at night. 'You can come back any Thursday,' she said. Saurabh pocketed the mint.

qa.q: What did Mrs Pillai write down for Saurabh?
qa.a: A helpline run by trained counsellors and the name of a book in the school library.

qa.q: What was Saurabh feeling as he turned the mint over?
qa.a: He felt scared and confused about his feelings for Tejas, unsure there was even a word for them.

qa.q: What did Mrs Pillai's response get right?
qa.a: She stayed calm, said nothing was wrong with him, removed pressure to label, and pointed him to reliable information and a safe place to return.

qa.q: What would change if Saurabh had only kept watching random videos at night?
qa.a: He might take in confusing or frightening messages alone, instead of calm facts from a safe adult.

grounding: Shows a teen confused and afraid about attraction who finds a safe counsellor, is told no label is needed yet, and gets reliable information.

passage:
Subject: can I ask you something, Didi?
Dear Rekha Didi,
You said at Eid I could write to you about anything, so here goes. I'm confused about myself and it's scaring me. Everyone in my class talks about which boy they like, and I just nod along. Sometimes I think I feel that way about a girl in my dance class, then I'm not sure at all, and then I lie awake worrying about what it means and what Abbu would say.
I looked things up online and it made it worse. Some pages shout, some make jokes.
Yesterday our school counsellor said in a talk that it's normal not to know yet, and you don't have to decide on a word. That helped. I wrote down the helpline she gave.
So I'm not asking you to tell me what I am. I just want one safe person to talk to while I figure it out. Video call on Sunday?
Zainab

qa.q: What did the school counsellor say in the talk?
qa.a: That it's normal not to know yet, and you don't have to decide on a word.

qa.q: What is Zainab worried about while lying awake?
qa.a: Zainab feels scared and confused about what the feelings mean and anxious about what Abbu would say.

qa.q: What did Zainab do that was wise?
qa.a: Stopped relying on confusing web pages, noted the counsellor's helpline, and reached out to one safe person without rushing a label.

qa.q: How might Rekha Didi feel reading the email?
qa.a: She would probably feel trusted and protective, glad Zainab turned to her, and want to listen rather than decide anything.

grounding: An email from a teen afraid and confused about attraction, choosing not to label quickly and turning to a safe person and reliable information.
